claims.text: Standard elemental Cr coatings provide strong oxidation protection on Zircaloy cladding.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of elemental Cr coatings on Zircaloy.
Controlled intermittent oxygen pulses during PVD will generate periodic Cr2O3 lamellae within a Cr coating.
The oxygen-pulsed process will produce a self-organized nanolaminate of alternating metallic Cr and Cr2O3 layers.
Ultrathin Cr2O3 lamellae within the coating will act as internal diffusion barriers.
Embedded Cr2O3 lamellae will reduce fast oxygen-diffusion paths.
Embedded Cr2O3 lamellae will reduce elemental migration through the coating.
Fragmenting the Cr phase into periodic microstructural units will limit Cr–Zr interdiffusion during high-temperature exposure.
The nanolaminate will preserve the oxidation resistance associated with elemental Cr.
The oxygen-pulsed nanolaminate coating will have greater oxidation resistance than an unmodified elemental Cr coating.
The oxygen-pulsed nanolaminate coating will exhibit less interfacial Cr–Zr mixing than an unmodified elemental Cr coating.
Reduced interfacial mixing will improve coating mechanical integrity and prolong service life.
The proposed coating will improve durability during extended subcritical-water service at approximately 300°C.
The proposed coating will improve durability during transient steam exposure up to approximately 1200°C for less than 30 minutes.
Excessive oxygen exposure or discontinuous oxide lamellae could compromise coating adhesion and barrier performance.
Performance under prolonged radiation and neutron exposure has not yet been established.
